Approach and Rationale

The primary goal is to minimize the AC1 upper bound, defined as 2n * max(convolve(a)) / (sum(a))^2, using step-function coefficients clipped between 0 and 1000. The supplied parent program uses gradient-based optimization with multiple initializations and local search steps. However, it requires dense matrix operations which may exceed memory limits for large n. Our strategy combines sparse initialization methods with gradient projection and adaptive budget allocation, leveraging the exact evaluator sparingly while maintaining validity.

Key improvements:

  • Algorithmic projection of gradients to enforce feasibility
  • Sparse initialization using FFT-based solvers
  • Adaptive budget scheduling to prevent timeout
  • Separate gradient verification steps

Mathematical Specification

Objective: Minimize upper_bound = 2 * len(a) * max(convolve(a, mode='full')) / (sum(a))**2 given:

  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000 for all i
  • sum(a) ≥ 0.01
